metaDescription: Free shadcn/ui theme generator. Create light and dark OKLCH CSS variables from a primary colour, neutral tint and radius, with @theme inline mapping.
intro: Generate the CSS variables for a shadcn/ui theme from a primary colour, a neutral tint and a border radius. Light and dark modes are included in OKLCH, with the @theme inline mapping.
why:
A shadcn/ui theme is a long list of CSS variables: background, foreground, card, popover, primary, secondary, muted, accent, destructive, border, input, ring, chart colours and sidebar tokens, each with a light and a dark value. Building a coherent set by hand takes a while, and a single poorly chosen foreground can make text unreadable.

Choose a primary colour, a neutral tint such as slate, zinc or stone, and a radius. The tool derives the rest, picks light or dark foreground text for the primary, creates dark-mode variants, and adds chart colours around the hue wheel. The @theme inline block maps the variables to Tailwind colour names. The result is a starting point, so check contrast in your own components. Nothing is uploaded.
howTo: Choose a neutral tint: neutral, slate, zinc, stone or match primary.
Set the radius, for example 0.625rem, and keep @theme inline ticked for Tailwind v4.
Copy the CSS into your global stylesheet and look at the light and dark preview.

faq.a: The variable names and OKLCH values follow the current shadcn/ui and Tailwind v4 conventions, including the @theme inline block. For older setups, you may need to adjust the format.

faq.q: How is the foreground colour chosen?
faq.a: For the primary colour, the tool uses dark text when the colour is light and near-white text when it is dark. Check contrast with the contrast checker for your actual components.

faq.q: What does the neutral tint change?
faq.a: It sets the hue and a small amount of colour in greys such as background, border and muted. Neutral is pure grey, while slate and others add a slight cool or warm tone.
Yes, all values are plain CSS variables. Adjust any token, then keep light and dark pairs consistent so the interface stays readable.
